thread:
nina.docs: Quick note — our Node quickstart README still shows an env var called REDWOOD_SCOPE_VAR in the example. New users copy/paste and immediately see 403s.

ira.support: Yep saw 3 tickets today about this. They all had keys scoped for embeddings only and tried the text-generation example.

nina.docs: Problematic snippet from README: 
```bash
# BAD
export REDWOOD_SCOPE_VAR=inference.generate
node quickstart.js
```
This implies users should set a scope env var; actually you must set an API key that already has scopes. Proposed replacement: 
```bash
# GOOD
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_...
node quickstart.js
```
And add a Troubleshooting -> "check your token scopes" with a curl example.

alex.sdk: I'll update the SDK error handling so 403 includes a hint: "403 Forbidden — token missing required scope (inference.generate). See https://docs.redwood.ai/auth#scopes". Also will ensure client retry middleware does not retry on 401/403. I'll add a unit test to cover that.

nina.docs: Can you also add a one-line pseudo CLI to create a demo key so users know which scope to pick? Something like: `redwood keys create --scopes inference.generate --name quickstart-demo` (pseudo). We'll call that out as "dashboard/CLI example, not production advice".

alex.sdk: Yep. Creating SDK PR for better error text and retry fix. Will link the docs PR.

support-bot: Ticket #4821 linked to this thread. Docs PR opened by nina.docs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/501

ira.support: Thanks — once docs PR merges can we run the quickstart example on staging and confirm no auth-loop? That should stop these tickets.

nina.docs: Will add the curl check (`curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tokens/me`) and a short scope matrix (generation vs embeddings) in the README.

alex.sdk: PRs incoming. I'll follow up with the SDK issue link in the docs so users can find the enriched error behavior.
